title: Agents of change

draft.title: Agents of change
card: Social change is a shift in how people live, think or relate to each other. An agent of change is anything that helps bring that shift about.
one person with a new idea, or a group acting together, can change attitudes or laws. Social movements and community organisations are examples.
new technologies change how people work, learn and communicate. Economic shifts, such as the growth or loss of an industry, can change where and how people live.
events such as wars can change a society quickly. They may alter who works, who holds power and how people see the world.
draft.remember: Change can come from people, groups, technology, the economy or events, and often from more than one at once.

a.q: A country's main factory industry closes and many families move to cities to find work. Which agent of change is this?
a.why: The loss of an industry is an economic shift, and it changed where people live. Nothing in the case is a new invention, so technology is not the agent here, even though factories use machines.
a.clue: Think about jobs and industry, not inventions.

b.q: In a town in Peru, a group of mothers organises, lobbies the council and wins a ban on street vendors selling near schools. Which agent of change best explains the new rule?
opts: A war or other major event
b.why: The change came from people organising and pressing for it, so the agent is a group. The vendors' trade has an economic side, but the rule was won by the mothers' action, not caused by a shift in the economy.
b.clue: Ask who actually made the change happen.
